== Biography ==
John Glasgow was the son of [[Glasgow-3135|Henry Glasgow]], a farmer. John was also a farmer and was living at Killycurragh, County Tyrone, in 1850.

On 16 June 1850, at Third Cookstown Presbyterian Church, John married [[Little-17961|Matilda Little]] of Drumeen, a daughter of Robert Little. Henry Glasgow and Archibald Little witnessed the marriage.<ref name="JohnMarriage1850">General Register Office of Ireland, civil marriage register, John Glasgow and Matilda Little, 16 June 1850, Cookstown registration district; [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1850/09386/5399841.pdf original register image], entry 39.</ref>

Matilda died in 1894 while still recorded as married.

== Research Notes ==
No matching 1901 census entry has been found for John.

The ''Tyrone Courier'' reported in February 1898 that an 86-year-old farmer named John Glasgow had died suddenly at Killycurragh. He had been a member of First Presbyterian Church and was found dead by his servant.<ref>[https://www.britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk/viewer/bl/0001693/18980210/088/0004 ''Tyrone Courier''], 10 February 1898, p. 4.</ref> No matching civil death registration has been located. This report is the basis of the estimated birth and death dates, but the identification remains uncertain.

John has also been considered as the unnamed married nephew living with [[Glasgow-1022|John Glasgow]] at Glenleslie, County Antrim, in 1851. The 1850 marriage instead places this John at Killycurragh in County Tyrone and names his father as Henry Glasgow.<ref name="JohnMarriage1850" /> No record makes Henry a brother of John Glasgow of Glenleslie. The shared name and approximate age therefore do not establish that they were the same person.

A possible identification concerns John Glasgow, Drogheda sub-constable, 1850. Sub-constable John Glasgow, explicitly of the Drogheda police, appears in a court report on 19 October 1850. He found the prisoner running away with a bag of meal in an oatmeal-theft case. John is the police witness, not the accused.<ref>The Drogheda Argus and Leinster Journal, 19 October 1850, p.2, court theft report; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/1259561281/ record].</ref> Occupation and police station are explicit; age, birthplace, relatives and exact service dates are unstated. [[Glasgow-2056]], [[Glasgow-2537]] and [[Glasgow-867]] are adult chronology comparisons only, with no checked constabulary connection. An administrative Drogheda probate label on a different John lead is not evidence of Drogheda residence or police service. Royal Irish Constabulary service records and local directories are the next identity tests. The identification remains uncertain.

A possible identification concerns John Glasgow, Dundrum subscription-list context, 1840. John Glasgow occurs in the Loyal National Repeal Association subscription report, under “Per Mr. Edward Byrne, Dundrum,” published on 19 October 1840. This is a personal surname occurrence in a named collection list.<ref>Freeman’s Journal and Daily Commercial Advertiser, 19 October 1840, p.4, Loyal National Repeal Association subscriptions; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/1050137248/ record]; Freeman’s Journal and Daily Commercial Advertiser, 19 October 1840, p. 4, Loyal National Repeal Association subscriptions (alternate scan); [https://www.newspapers.com/image/1380778107/ record].</ref> The list supplies no age, occupation, exact address, relatives or individual subscription amount. Dundrum identifies the collection context; it is not an explicit statement of John’s residence. [[Glasgow-2058]], [[Glasgow-1968]] and [[Glasgow-2056]] survive as chronology comparisons only; none has a checked Dublin or Dundrum bridge. No identification or religious affiliation is inferred from the political subscription. Image 1380778107 is an alternate scan of this same report and list passage, not a second occurrence. The identification remains uncertain.
